bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in format_expand1 OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=498472071 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: format_expand1 format_expand format-fuzzer.c ```
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / default_crash_trace.txt / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is exactly one byte, `0x23` (`"#"`). The fuzz harness allocates `size + 1`, copies that byte, appends a NUL terminator, and calls `format_expand()` with the two-byte heap string `"#\0"`. In vulnerable `format_expand1()`, the `#` parser branch executes `if (*fmt++ == '\0')` after already confirming `*fmt == '#'`, so the condition tests the current `'#'` byte instead of checking whether a following byte exists. The branch therefore does not stop on a terminal `#`; it advances `fmt` onto the in-bounds terminator, `ch = (u_char)*fmt++` consumes that NUL and moves `fmt` one byte past the 2-byte allocation, the default case continues the loop, and the next `while (*fmt != '\0')` header dereferences the one-past-end pointer. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at that loop header. The fix changes the check to `if (*++fmt == '\0')`, which tests the post-`#` character before the later dereference can advance past the buffer.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled format string and chooses the `#`-specific parsing path needed for the bug.
source.value_from: The staged PoC file is exactly one byte `0x23` (`"#"`). The harness copies that byte into a heap buffer of length 2 and appends `buf[1] = '\0'`, so project code receives the exact string `"#\0"` and `*fmt == '#'` at this statement.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than the libFuzzer entry point because it is the first project statement that reads the attacker-controlled format byte and creates the branch state used by the vulnerable path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The terminal-`#` emptiness check tests the current `'#'` byte and advances the pointer, instead of first moving to and validating the byte after `#`.
root_cause.note: Because step 2 already established `*fmt == '#'`, this predicate is always false for the one-byte witness and still increments `fmt` to the terminator. The fix changes it to `*++fmt`, expressing the missing post-`#` bounds check.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The loop header dereferences `fmt` after previous logic has advanced it one byte past the 2-byte heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `format_expand1` at `format.c:5457:9`, with the 2-byte allocation originating from `malloc(size + 1)` in `fuzz/format-fuzzer.c:43`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness copies the one-byte witness into a heap buffer and appends the NUL terminator that makes the vulnerable parser state `"#\0"`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The PoC bytes are exactly `23`. With `size == 1`, the harness allocates 2 bytes, writes `buf[0] = '#'`, then writes `buf[1] = '\0'` before passing `buf` to `format_expand()`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact one-byte witness passes the fuzz target's non-empty and size limit gate, so the format string is admitted for expansion.

fine_trace.note: After lines 43-47 allocate `size + 1`, copy the exact one-byte witness `0x23`, and append `buf[size] = '\0'`, the harness passes the 2-byte heap string `"#\0"` into project code.
Source. The first attacker-controlled byte is `'#'`, so this branch is false and execution enters the parser logic that treats `#` as the start of a format escape instead of copying it literally.

Root cause. This check still examines the current `'#'` byte, so it cannot detect that the `#` is terminal. It nevertheless increments `fmt`, leaving the pointer on the in-bounds NUL terminator instead of breaking out before later post-`#` parsing.
With `fmt` now on the terminator from step 3, this statement reads the in-bounds NUL byte into `ch` and advances `fmt` to one byte past the 2-byte heap allocation.

Because `ch == '\0'` does not match any recognized `#` escape, the default case takes the `s == NULL` arm, appends `'#'` and NUL to the output buffer, and `continue`s without restoring `fmt` or terminating the loop. Execution therefore returns to the loop header with `fmt` already one past the allocation.
Sink. The next loop iteration dereferences `*fmt` after step 4 moved `fmt` one byte past the 2-byte heap buffer and step 5 continued the loop, producing the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

format.name: tmux format string
format.contract: The witness is exactly one byte `0x23` (`"#"`). The harness appends a NUL terminator, so project code receives the 2-byte string `"#\0"` whose lone trailing `#` exercises the terminal-escape edge case.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and its line map matches the saved ASan frames at `format.c:5457` and `format.c:5608`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 is source-grounded. The saved artifacts prove the exact one-byte witness, the ASan crash location, the 2-byte allocation site, and the fix hunk, but they do not include an execution log of local variables after `switch (ch)` beyond what is recoverable directly from source.
